title: Fasolakia
subtitle: Greek green beans braised in olive oil and tomato
excerpt: Green beans cooked slowly in olive oil until completely tender, with tomato, garlic and dill. A Greek ladera dish that is served at room temperature as a main or side.
sourceNotes: Greek ladera (olive-oil-braised vegetable) tradition, found across the country as a summer staple.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales easily. Cook in a wider pan so the beans sit in a single layer.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a few hours ahead and eaten at room temperature. Keeps refrigerated for three days.

content.text: Fasolakia is a ladera dish: vegetables braised in generous olive oil until soft all the way through. The beans should be fully tender, not crisp. Serve warm or at room temperature with bread to mop up the oil.
Warm the olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tinned tomatoes, water, salt and pepper. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Add the potatoes if using. Stir to coat. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the green beans and stir well. The sauce should almost cover them. Top up with a little water if needed.
Cover and cook on a low heat for 35 minutes. The beans should be completely soft, not al dente.
Stir in the dill. Taste and adjust the salt. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The beans are still firm after 35 minutes.
items.cause: The heat was too high and the liquid evaporated before the beans had time to soften.
items.fix: Add a splash of water, cover and continue cooking for 10 to 15 more minutes on a lower heat.

items.cause: The lid was kept on and water did not evaporate.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer for 10 minutes to reduce the sauce to a thicker, oily consistency.

items.cause: Not enough salt or the dill was missed.
items.fix: Add salt and a squeeze of lemon. Stir in fresh dill if it was not added at the end.
